question: In Ontario, can my landlord evict me just by handing me an eviction notice?
generated_answer: In Ontario, a landlord cannot evict you just by handing you an eviction notice. You can only be evicted by a court order. The landlord must apply to the Landlord and Tenant Board (LTB) for an order of eviction. The LTB will hold a hearing to decide whether you should be evicted. If the LTB decides that you should be evicted, it will issue an order of eviction. The order of eviction will specify the date by which you must leave the rental unit. If you do not leave the rental unit by the specified date, the landlord can apply to the LTB for an order of possession. The order of possession will allow the landlord to take possession of the rental unit and evict you. It is important to note that the landlord cannot evict you without a court order. If the landlord tries to evict you without a court order, you can contact the LTB or a lawyer for assistance.
